heading: multiview MU — silhouette guard: a slender solid does not follow a `loft`
text: Cause found and repair prepared and measured; NOT landed (the same constraint as the pocket rule: the module decides all 385 assets, and no fixer may be measuring against it meanwhile). Reproduced with the lofts of `🧰️matrix/MX-2/loft.ts` (`ops/bentwood-500.lofts.json`: the four bones of the chairs `b` and `d`, 10 views, 0 refused; `loft.ts used-bentwood-dining-chairs --ops … --out trial.json`): front IoU 1:500 0.9118 (limit 0.92; yours 0.9050, the lofts differ in detail), drawn 33,444 cells, volume 34,695, both 32,499. Cause: the volume side is a stroke of ONE width per slender solid, twice the 90th percentile of the vertex distances (`strokesOf`, `truth`), while the loft tapers from 21 to 30 mm, so the volume is 1,251 cells (3.7 %) larger than the drawing. A constant mean width instead gives 0.9202, a number on the limit, so the width is not the point. The rule that fits your sentence: `drawsBody(bone, centre, drawn, material, truth)` (nine tenths of the projected centre line inside a filled closed drawn shape of the bone and material, or within half the true width of its outline) makes `strokesOf` return the projected triangles of the solid itself, tapering included. Measured on the trial module (`🧰️matrix/MX-2/pocket/silhouette.ts`, the pocket rule included; `pocket/where.ts 500 <view> <trial.json>`): front 0.9118 to **0.9464** (drawn 33,444, volume 33,445), plan 0.9953 to 0.9954, elevation 0.9263 to 0.9447; the document without lofts is unchanged (0.9412 in both, 1:50 to 1:200 unchanged). The rule needs the lofts `filled` (a body): the paint rule of `loft.ts` copies `filled` from the shape it replaces, and the old strokes are unfilled, so an ops entry may say `"filled": true` now (tool change, optional). Four failing-first cases (`pocket/test.ts`: 13 of 13 on the trial copy, 6 of 13 on the live module). After the landing: `python3 🧰️matrix/MU/make/used-bentwood-dining-chairs.py --with-500` with filled lofts, `apply.sh used-bentwood-dining-chairs` and the proofs. Until then the asset stays repaired at 1:50, 1:100 and 1:200 only, as you have it. Whole-suite check and the other assets measured: `multiview-MX-2.md`, section on the pocket rule.
